title: Decide what a Done row promises when a hardlink correction lands later, and show it or stop implying finality
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Assert.NotEqual() Failure: Strings are equal — Expected: Not "1-folder", Actual: "1-folder" (DoneRowFinalityTests.cs:line 66)
The 'Done is immutable' UI/data problem has been decided and fixed: the row is shown differently (or Done's promise is otherwise resolved) when a hardlink correction lands after settling: missing

report-captures-mid-scan-done-row: needs first: To check a chosen Done wording/suffix this way, two things would need to be added first: a new FsaWindowHook mode that reads/logs the window (or triggers a report-like snapshot) before E…

Does 'show it, don't imply finality' cover only the top-level list rows the failing test and validate's C:\Windows observation describe, or should folder-tree drill-down nodes (built from ScanStore after the scan) also carry a revision mark? This design covers only the top-level list, matching the bug's own framing ('the window prints no suffix'), but a person could decide the promise should extend to the tree view too.

The exact suffix wording "(revised)" versus an alternative like "(updated)" or "(corrected)" is unsettled cosmetics -- the proposal itself calls it changeable in an hour and picked it only for consistency with the existing "(reading...)" style.

No revision mark in the folder tree. The design's open question (tree coverage) stays open for a person. Note that a Completed scan replaces the results list with the tree (measured: the published exe's report on the repro tree shows FolderTree visible and TopLevelList with 0 realised rows). So the mark is visible only while a scan runs (in practice the probe pass) and after a Cancel.

No change to the --report schema 1 and no FsaWindowHook mode, as designed, because spike report-captures-mid-scan-done-row was no-go. Window-level proof is the in-process MainWindow test (C-008), not the shipped report.
No test for C-009 (a correction landing in the same ~250 ms interval the row first became Done). It is non-material and the design accepts it as over-marking; the settled capture marks such a row.

Person decision still open: should folder-tree nodes carry a revision mark? On a completed scan the tree replaces the list, so today the mark never appears after a successful ending. On a small tree (the repro finished in 23 ms) it is never on screen at all.
Wording '(revised)' versus '(updated)' or '(corrected)' is still unsettled cosmetics. It is changed in one place, TopLevelRowText.TitleOf, and TheMarkShowsOnlyOnADoneRow's InlineData.
The `\.Revised\b` App rule misses a property-pattern read such as `row is { Revised: true }`. A `\bRevised\b` pattern with the same exception would close that gap.

An Unreadable top-level row whose partial listing is later probe-corrected moves its figures with no mark, because the design scoped the mark to Done. Worth a decision if Unreadable rows are meant to read as settled too.

Measured at build, relevant to criterion 6 and SL-056: a scan's metadata probe through a stale hardlink name makes NTFS refresh that name's directory entry. `dir` showed stale.bin at 1,048,576 before a scan and 67,108,864 after, and a second scan corrected nothing. It is not a timestamp change as far as observed, but the scan does alter what the next listing sees. Any test using the stale-name shape needs a fresh tree per run.

If window-level proof through the shipped exe is ever wanted, the smallest step is an aggregate revised-row count in the report (no names, per Q-016) plus a hook mode that reports before EndingShown, as the risk spike found.

not reached: On a Completed scan the folder tree replaces the list. On real ProgramData the mark was drawn for about 200 ms before the tree replaced it, so a person rarely sees it unless they press Stop. Whether tree nodes should carry the mark is the open person decision.

not reached: Outside the 10 criteria, for a person: the scanning header says only 'Rows marked reading are still growing', but Done rows moved by up to 1.79 GB on-disk during the probe pass. After a Cancel during the probe pass, Done rows keep unprobed listing figures with no mark: this cancelled run's on-disk total was about 748 MB below the completed run's. Yet the header says only not-read or stopped-partway rows are short. That is a residual implication of finality that nothing marks.
